Explain how a VPN works in simple words
6:41 PM

A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet: everything you send is locked first, passes through the tunnel to a VPN company's computer, and only then goes out to the website you wanted.

What that does for you:

Your internet provider, or the café Wi-Fi, sees only scrambled data, not which sites you visit.
Websites see the VPN computer's location instead of yours, so your real address stays hidden.
On public Wi-Fi, strangers on the same network can't read what you send.

What it doesn't do: it doesn't make you fully anonymous. The VPN company can see your traffic, so pick one you trust. It also won't protect you from fake links or weak passwords.
